Raibhī, fem. plur., occurs in the Rigveda and the taittirīya Saṃhitā, together with gāthā and nārāśaṃsī, as a form of literature. Later on the raibhī verses are identified with certain verses of the Atharvaveda, but that this identification holds in the Rigveda and the taittirīya Saṃhitā seems very doubtful.

Raibhya, ‘descendant of rebha,’ is the name of a teacher in the first two Vaṃśas (lists of teachers) in the Mādhyaṃdina recension of the Bṛhadāraṇyaka upaniṣad (ii. 5, 20; iv. 5, 26), where he is said to be a pupil of pautimāṣyāyaṇa and kauṇḍinyāyana.
